title: Thinking Loop v5: depth allocation and best defence

D0.outcome: Explains why the deepest thought goes to critical, forcing, irreversible decisions and why routine moves get little.

D1.outcome: For a position, says which candidate deserves the deepest calculation and gives the reason (forcing, irreversible, unique).

D2.outcome: Within a stated time budget on a set of positions, spends longer on the critical ones and shorter on routine ones, as shown by the time log.

D3.outcome: Before accepting a line, checks the opponent's best defence at each leaf including quiet defensive moves, and finds the refutation in positions where the first-choice line has one.

D4.outcome: In own games, a depth-versus-worth log shows time and depth following the importance of the move; the share of long thinks on routine moves falls over ten games.

misconceptions: Thinking longer always improves the move.
Analysis ends when my line works; the opponent's reply is his problem.

contrasts: Stopping at the first line that works; the master rejected a combination as unsound and let it be played because he missed a quiet follow-up.
A deep think on a move with an obvious only-reply.
A quiet maneuvering position with no critical decision in sight.
